title: Keel's Save Instance measures deposits under the partner's former name, exposing a dependency on legacy identifiers in external data
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.5.2.2.3.1.5 repeats the standard Integration Boost data clause and then adds an exception: "the data for Save is available through the API endpoint under Solend, the previous name Save operated under."

This is a small provision with a general lesson. The Artifact's payment logic depends on an external dataset it does not control, and that dataset is keyed by a name that has since changed. Rather than treating the mismatch as an operational detail for whoever runs the process, the Atlas writes the aliasing into the governing document — so an operator reading only the Artifact does not look up "Save," find nothing, and conclude the deposits were zero.

The choice is honest but fragile. Documenting the legacy key in `[Core]` text means correcting it later requires a Root Edit, and it hard-codes into Keel's constitution a naming artefact of a third-party analytics provider. The alternative — normalizing the data upstream — would have kept the Artifact clean but moved the discrepancy somewhere less visible.

The wider point for anyone auditing incentive programs: identity drift in partners (rebrands, mergers, contract migrations) silently breaks measurement pipelines that key on names, and the failure mode looks like an absence of activity rather than an error.
description: The Artifact records that Save's figures appear in the shared incentives API under 'Solend', so the payment pipeline keys on a superseded name rather than the partner's current identity.
